entries.german: Sigmund widerruft auf Veranlassung des Ulrich v. Rosenberg eine von dem Karlsteiner Burggr. Zdeslaus ausgestellte Urkunde. („Sigismundus ... notum facimus ..., quod nobilis Ulricus de Rosenberg ... accessivit majestatem nostram et informavit nos, quod, dum castrum nostrum Clingberg exsolvit cum suis bonis et paratis pecuniis ex mandato nostro, quod propter quandam literam quam dedimus Mathie Brus, cui obligavimus pro serviciis suis, que fecit nobis in obsidione castri nostri Karlstein, cui proscripcionem fecimus in villis claustri nostri Milocensis, que ville hic in ista litera nominibus suis sunt descripte, scilicet Lhota et Dobrussow vocatas ac curiam allodialem in Kowarzow habitam cum tribus censitis, item alias villas Hraykrowicz Piedl Wladyczin et Dmyssticz vocatas monasterii de Milewsk simul cum omnibus ipsarum proventibus ..., sicut in litera eius desuper confecta lacius continetur; et informans nos, quomodo Kunat noluit sibi castrum condescendere dicens, quod Johannes Przedbor habet literam istam obligacionis nostre et quod ipse est commissarius Brussonis pie memorie, et isti, quos misit ad eum sicut Nicolaum de Hrchleb et alios de consilio suo, ut intromitterent se de castro, oportebat eos componere cum Johanne Przedbor, ut annuatim darent sibi certam summam pecuniarum usque ad exsolucionem trecentarum sexagenarum, sicut in litera nostra inpignoratum est. Et nos audientes ista fecimus querere in registris nostris et invenimus, quod Zdeslaus purgravius noster in Karlstein sicut vendidit aliqua clenodia nostra, que habuimus ibi, pro solucione dampnorum istis, qui fuerunt cum eo in obsidione et in serviciis suis, et eciam exsolvit ab illo supradicto Mathia ista bona supradicta per nos sibi obligata. Et nos considerantes hoc, si ista litera inviolata et observata esset, eam cassamus irritamus et nullius vigoris facimus. In cuius rei testimonium sigillum nostrum mediante [!] jussimus apponere. Datum Feldkirchen feria secunda post nativitatem s. Marie virginis anno domini millesimo quadringentesimo tricesimo, regnorum nostrorum anno Hungarie 44., Romanorum 20., Boemie decimo[!]) Ad mandatum domini regis Caspar Sligk
entries.english: At the instigation of Ulrich von Rosenberg, Sigismund revokes a charter issued by Zdeslaus, Burgrave of Karlstein. (“Sigismund ... make known ... that the noble Ulrich von Rosenberg ... came to our Majesty and informed us that, when he redeemed our castle of Clingberg with his own goods and ready money by our command because of a certain charter we had granted to Mathias Brus, to whom we had pledged [property] for his services to us during the siege of our castle Karlstein, where we had imposed a ban on villages of our monastery of Miloc, which villages are named in this charter as Lhota and Dobrussow, and on the demesne court at Kowarzow with three rent-paying holdings, and likewise on other villages of the monastery of Milewsko named Hraykrowicz, Piedl, Wladyczin, and Dmyssticz, together with all their revenues ..., as is set out more fully in the charter drawn up for him; and he informed us how Kunat refused to yield the castle to him, saying that Johannes Przedbor held this charter of our pledge and was the agent of the late Brus, and that those whom he had sent to Kunat, including Nicolaus de Hrchleb and others of his council, to take possession of the castle, had been obliged to come to terms with Johannes Przedbor, agreeing to pay him a fixed sum each year until the redemption of 300 schock, as is pledged in our charter. When we heard this, we had our registers searched and found that Zdeslaus, our burgrave at Karlstein, had sold some of our jewels kept there to pay the damages owed to those who had been with him at the siege and in his service, and had also redeemed from the aforesaid Mathias the aforesaid property which we had pledged to him. Considering this, if that charter were to remain in force and be observed, we hereby cancel and annul it and declare it to be of no effect. In witness whereof we have ordered our seal to be affixed. Given at Feldkirchen on Monday after the Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, in the year of the Lord 1430, in the 44th year of our reign in Hungary, the 20th in the Romans' realm, and the 10th in Bohemia.” By the hand of the lord king, Caspar Sligk.)
